purpose: Backfill Notion-spec required .agent-os/ files (loop.md, harness.md) that were missing from initial Week 1 deliverables. Also introduce the JSON batch-plan pattern for multi-file change planning.
rationale: Notion spec at https://www.notion.so/36085ab46da8813f8cfee6d5982ec0d0 specifies .agent-os/{context-template.md, loop.md, harness.md} as the minimal Agent OS kit for Week 1.
We previously created only context-template.md. loop.md and harness.md were missing, leaving the Notion-defined deliverable incomplete.
User asked whether JSON could help manage parallel work — this file demonstrates the pattern.

design_principles.scope: per-batch planning artifact, persisted alongside the change for audit
design_principles.ownership: human-authored or AI-drafted before execution, reviewed once, then frozen as historical record

operations.content_summary: Slim iteration procedure (4 phases) pointing to task-context-flow + tdd-endpoint Skills and harness.md.
Verification checklist: automated (gradle test) + manual (per task) + failure-mode questions.
This very file — batch plan as artifact + demo of JSON-for-parallel pattern.

operations.change: Append a line after step 4 pointing to .agent-os/loop.md, harness.md, and batches/ JSON pattern.

parallel_execution.strategy: single function_calls block with 4 independent invokes — 3 Writes + 1 Edit, no inter-operation dependencies
parallel_execution.sequential_fallback: if any invoke fails (e.g., Edit text mismatch), rerun only the failed one

verification: git status confirms 4 paths changed (3 new + 1 modified)
Re-read AGENTS.md to confirm pointer integrated cleanly into Task workflow section
future_uses_of_batch_pattern: Cross-cutting refactors (e.g., renaming a contract across controllers/tests/docs)
Pre-implementation reviews where the operations list itself is part of the discussion
